definition: A hydrocarbon reservoir only accumulates where an impermeable rock layer sits above a source of decaying organic material, trapping the migrating fuel instead of letting it disperse to the surface.
core_idea: Without a sealing rock barrier, oil and gas would simply leak away over geologic time; the presence of the right rock formation is therefore what geologists search for, using seismic mapping to build 3D underground images before confirming a prospect with a test well.
key_points: An impermeable rock cap over decaying plant material is required to form a trappable reservoir.
Seismic waves are used to build three-dimensional maps of candidate underground formations.
Test wells are drilled into promising formations to confirm the actual presence of fuel before further development.
relationships: Depends on the same overpressure/heat/buoyancy migration mechanisms; the rock cap is what stops that migration at a producible depth.
